## Summary

The May 1 and November 7, 2026 captures describe customer-initiated installments on Mexican consumer credit cards. The cardholder’s bank collects installments over multiple billing statements. The merchant receives the purchase proceeds net of fees as with a standard card charge, on standard payout timing.

## Eligibility and installment fees

Stripe determines eligibility after payment method setup. The merchant needs a Stripe Mexico account. The customer must pay in MXN above the applicable plan minimum with a Mexico-issued consumer credit card from a supported issuer. Corporate cards are excluded. May labels the property **Customer locations** and November labels it **Card issuing country**. Both captures expressly require a Mexico-issued card.

Both captures give the same default minimums and fees. The installment fee is additional to the standard credit card transaction fee. In the Dashboard, select the plans to enable and configure custom minimum and maximum amounts for each plan.

| Months | Default minimum | Additional fee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | 300 MXN | 5% |
| 6 | 600 MXN | 7.5% |
| 9 | 900 MXN | 10% |
| 12 | 1,200 MXN | 12.5% |
| 18 | 1,800 MXN | 17.5% |
| 24 | 2,400 MXN | 22.5% |

## Issuers by capture

The May capture lists **32 issuers**. It limits Banamex to 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. The list comprises Afirme, American Express, Banamex, BanBajío, Banca Mifel, Banco Azteca, Banco Famsa, Banco Invex, Banco Multiva, Bancoppel, Banjercito, Banorte, Banregio, BBVA, Caja Morelia Valladolid, CrediClub, Didi, Efevoo Pay, Falabella, Hey Banco, Inbursa, Klar, Konfio, Liverpool, MercadoPago, NanoPay, Nubank, RappiCard, Santander, Scotiabank, Stori, and Suburbia.

The November capture lists **35 distinct issuers** across 36 entries.

| Listed plans in months | Issuers |
| --- | --- |
| 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24 | American Express, BBVA, Nubank |
| 3, 6, 9, 12, 18 | Afirme, Banamex, BanBajío, Banca Mifel, Banco Azteca, Banco Invex, Banco Multiva, Banjercito, Banorte, Banregio, Caja Morelia Valladolid, CrediClub, Efevoo Pay, Falabella, Hey Banco, HSBC, Inbursa, Klar, Konfio, Liverpool, NanoPay, RappiCard, Santander, Scotiabank, Suburbia |
| 3, 6, 9, 12 | Banco Plata, Bancoppel, Didi, Inbursa, MercadoPago, Revolut, Stori, Ualá |

Banamex appears in the through-18-month group. Banco Plata, HSBC, Revolut, and Ualá are newly listed. The November list omits Banco Famsa. Inbursa appears in both the through-12-month and through-18-month groups, leaving its 18-month availability unresolved. An issuer’s listing alone leaves actual card and plan eligibility unverified.

## Integration routes and payment states

Both captures list the Payment Intents and Payment Methods APIs, Checkout, Invoicing, Payment Element, and Payment Links. November also lists [[stripe-terminal|Terminal]]. The separate November Mexico acceptance capture supplies a Terminal variant link. Reader support, SDK behavior, charge types, and account availability require evidence from the applicable product and SDK documentation.

Stripe-hosted payments display eligible installment plans after the customer enters a supported card number. The overview recommends the same order for a custom payment UI. Card entry and plan display precede authorization, capture, and merchant payout. Both overview captures route their hosted UI and Direct API example links to Japan. Use the separate [[source-stripe-mx-installments-accept-payment|Mexico acceptance guide]] for Mexico integration and test cards. Its November variant index supplies navigation.

Both overview captures list recurring payments, disputes, manual capture, and full and partial refunds as supported properties. The May Mexico acceptance guide limits hosted Checkout installments to `payment` mode, excluding `setup` and `subscription`. It limits Invoicing installments to individual invoices, excluding subscriptions. Apply those limits to their documented paths.

Connect platforms can process installments on behalf of connected accounts and set the default installment configuration for accounts in Mexico. Standard connected accounts can override it in the Dashboard.

payments-mx-installments.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mx-installments, the November capture describes Mexican installments as customer-initiated credit-card payments. Eligibility requires a Stripe Mexico account, an MXN amount above the applicable plan minimum, and a consumer credit card from a supported Mexican issuer. Stripe determines eligibility after setup. The bank collects installments from the customer, while the merchant receives the purchase proceeds net of fees on standard payout timing. A hosted UI displays options after a supported card number, and the overview recommends a comparable order for a custom UI. Displayed plans and card entry precede a payment outcome (old raw lines 4-56 and old raw lines 58-100, new raw lines 5-57 and new raw lines 59-101). Fees and default minima remain aligned across the six plans, with Dashboard configuration and a Standard connected-account override. November adds Terminal and groups issuers by plan duration. Banamex moves from 12 to 18 months at the top of its documented range, while the duplicate Inbursa placement leaves that issuer's 18-month availability unclear. The mapped source-stripe-mx-installments.md summarizes May's fees and requirements and names Banamex's historical limit, but counts 33 issuers compared with 32 listed in May (old raw lines 102-137 and new raw lines 103-150). The revised source dates the issuer lists separately and records 35 distinct November names across 36 entries.
payments-mx-installments.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mx-installments, the substantive November changes missing from source-stripe-mx-installments.md are the Terminal product listing and issuer-specific plan groups. American Express, BBVA and Nubank are placed in the 24-month group, Banamex joins the 18-month group, and Banco Plata, HSBC, Revolut and Ualá are newly listed. Banco Famsa is absent. Keep the May issuer list and Banamex restriction dated, correct the baseline count from 33 to 32 names, and warn reciprocally that November lists Inbursa in both the 12- and 18-month groups. The country property changes from customer location to card issuing country while both captures already require a Mexico-issued card. Fee table formatting and headings are presentational (old raw lines 12-20, old raw lines 78-100 and old raw lines 102-137, new raw lines 13-21, new raw lines 79-101 and new raw lines 103-150). The retained hosted and Direct API links point to Japan, while the Mexico acceptance index has its own Mexico variants and a Terminal route. Keep that warning and preserve the broad recurring property alongside the dated Checkout payment-mode and individual-invoice limits. Product documentation, UI availability, card authorization or capture, issuer collection and ordinary merchant payout describe different stages (old raw lines 22-76 and new raw lines 23-77). The revised source routes to the Mexico acceptance guide and Terminal concept, and preserves the date-specific evidence boundaries.

concept_suggestions.anchor: Mexico-only consumer credit card installment feature. MX Stripe accounts only; MXN only; consumer cards only (no corporate). 6 plan options (3–24 months); merchant receives full amount **minus additional fees** (5%–22.5%); bank handles collection. 33 supported issuers including BBVA, Banorte, Santander, Amex, Nubank, Didi. Custom min/max amounts configurable. Connect supported. See [[source-stripe-mx-installments]] for fees table and full issuer list.
concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown:
Mexico installments require a Stripe Mexico account, payment in MXN above the plan minimum, and a Mexico-issued consumer credit card from a supported issuer. There are six plan lengths from 3 to 24 months, with 5%–22.5% added to the standard card fee. The customer repays the issuer over time, while the merchant receives proceeds net of fees on standard payout timing. Custom minimums and maximums are configurable in the Dashboard. Connect platforms set defaults, and Standard connected accounts can override them.

The May 2026 overview lists 32 issuers. The November overview lists 35 distinct names grouped by plan length, with Inbursa in both the 12- and 18-month groups. Its 18-month availability is unresolved. November adds Terminal at product level. The overview’s hosted and Direct API links lead to Japan. Use the separate [[source-stripe-mx-installments-accept-payment|Mexico guide]], which documents hosted Checkout in `payment` mode and Invoicing for individual invoices. Those May integration limits apply to their paths alongside the overview’s broad recurring-payments property. See [[source-stripe-mx-installments]] for dated issuer and fee details.

Stripe's in-person payment product. Enables businesses to accept card payments using physical card readers and unifies in-person payments with online payments in a single Stripe Dashboard. Works with Stripe Connect platforms.

The November 2026 [[source-stripe-mx-installments|Mexico installments overview]] lists Terminal for Stripe Mexico accounts.
